jobs.title: Treasury Operations Senior
jobs.location: Dallas, Texas, United States of America
jobs.description:
At Freddie Mac, our mission of Making Home Possible is what motivates us, and it’s at the core of everything we do. Since our charter in 1970, we have made home possible for more than 90 million families across the country. Join an organization where your work contributes to a greater purpose.

Position Overview:

The Senior Treasury Operations Support Senior will be a key member of the Wireroom within the Treasury Operations group in the Investment & Capital Markets Division. This position in Plano, TX primarily supports the timely and accurate processing and reporting of funds and security wires and plays an important role in reducing payment risk.

Our Impact:

Treasury Operations ensures cash activity is processed in accordance with regulatory and corporate guidelines for the entire company. Investments & Capital Markets is responsible for handling our mortgage-related investments portfolio, single-family securitization activities, and treasury function.

Your Impact:

- Execute and support daily processing of high-volume and/or high-risk funds and securities wires and ACH activity in support of the firm’s business lines, ensuring accuracy, timeliness, and policy adherence.
- Act as a senior escalation point for exceptions, investigations, and time-sensitive issues, coordinating with internal areas to drive same-day resolution.
- Perform and validate reconciliations with banks and clearing firms and identify recurring issues and root causes.
- Develop, enhance, and execute departmental controls and procedures impacting cash and securities processing; recommend control improvements to reduce payment risk and operational defects.
- Support audit/exam readiness by maintaining documentation, evidence, and control execution artifacts; assist with responses to inquiries as needed.
- Contribute to process improvement efforts (e.g., standardization, documentation, metrics, and automation ideas) to improve quality and throughput.

Qualifications:

- Bachelor’s Degree and/or equivalent professional experience and 5+ years of overall relevant experience
- 3-4 yrs in treasury operations, payments, cash management, or financial operations (or equivalent)
- Proficiency in Microsoft Office Suite, with extensive use of Excel (e.g., pivot tables, lookups; ability to analyze large datasets), experience with AI tools is a plus
- Strong banking and financial industry knowledge, including NACHA processes/rules and operational payment controls
- Understanding of Federal Reserve payment systems (e.g., Fedwire); familiarity with securities settlement concepts is a plus
- Demonstrated strong data analysis, attention to detail in a controlled environment

Keys to Success in this Role:

- Strong verbal and written communication skills, including the ability to communicate clearly during escalations and cutoff-driven situations.
- Strong analytical, critical thinking, and problem-solving skills with a root-cause mindset.
- Excellent organizational skills and ability to manage multiple priorities with accuracy.
- Highly motivated with a desire to learn, adapt, and improve processes.
- Customer/stakeholder oriented while maintaining strong risk discipline.
- Ability to work independently and collaboratively across various teams; comfortable serving as a go-to resource without formal people management responsibilities.

AI-Enabled Analytics Transformation

jobs.title: Senior Business Lead, Data Governance Strategy & Execution
jobs.location: McLean, Virginia, United States of America
jobs.description:
At Freddie Mac, our mission of Making Home Possible is what motivates us, and it’s at the core of everything we do. Since our charter in 1970, we have made home possible for more than 90 million families across the country. Join an organization where your work contributes to a greater purpose.

Position Overview:

The Multifamily Data organization is seeking a Senior Business Lead, Data Governance Strategy & Execution to help shape and execute the future of data governance across Multifamily.

As Multifamily expands self-service access to data and enables new analytics, automation, and AI capabilities, trusted and well-governed data has become a strategic business imperative. This role will lead efforts to evolve governance from manual processes and one-time reviews into scalable capabilities embedded within our data platform, data products, and delivery processes.

Working across business, technology, risk, privacy, compliance, and data teams, this leader will drive the strategy and execution needed to ensure Multifamily data is trusted, transparent, reusable, and fit for purpose. The role will also help establish the governance foundations necessary to support responsible AI adoption and ensure alignment between data governance and emerging AI governance requirements.

Our Impact:

Multifamily Data is transforming how data is managed, delivered, understood, and consumed across the business.

Our mission is to provide a trusted data foundation that enables better business decisions, operational efficiency, regulatory compliance, advanced analytics, and AI-driven innovation. Through modern data platforms, trusted data products, and strong governance practices, we are improving transparency, strengthening data quality, and making data easier to discover, understand, and use.

As Multifamily continues its data modernization journey, governance must evolve alongside the platform to ensure trust scales with growing volumes of data, consumers, analytics, and AI solutions.

Your Impact:

In this role, you will:
- Define and advance Multifamily's data governance strategy, roadmap, and operating model.

- Lead cross-functional initiatives that improve data quality, metadata management, data lineage, stewardship, ownership, and consumer trust.

- Partner with Data Product, Engineering, Architecture, and Platform teams to embed governance directly into the data lifecycle.

- Drive automation of governance capabilities, reducing reliance on manual oversight while increasing consistency and transparency.

- Establish scalable governance capabilities that support trusted self-service reporting, analytics, and data product consumption.

- Define and implement the data governance foundations needed to support responsible and effective AI adoption.

- Serve as a key connector between data governance and AI governance, ensuring appropriate controls, lineage, transparency, privacy, accountability, and data readiness standards are in place.

- Partner with Risk, Privacy, Compliance, Audit, and Regulatory stakeholders to ensure governance practices align with enterprise and regulatory expectations.

- Develop meaningful metrics that demonstrate improvements in data trust, governance maturity, consumer adoption, and AI readiness.

- Influence senior leaders and stakeholders to drive alignment and execution without direct authority.

Qualifications:
- Bachelor's degree plus relevant experience.

- 10+ years of experience in Data Governance, Data Management, Data Strategy, Data Quality, Data Risk Management, or a related discipline.

- Proven success leading large-scale, cross-functional initiatives through influence and collaboration.

- Strong understanding of data governance frameworks, metadata management, data lineage, data quality, stewardship, and data controls.

- Understanding of the relationship between data governance, AI governance, privacy, security, and responsible AI.

- Experience with metadata, data catalog, lineage, and data quality platforms.

- Experience with modern cloud data platforms, data products, and self-service analytics environments.

- Experience translating business, regulatory, and technology requirements into practical governance solutions.

- Experience collaborating across business, technology, risk, compliance, and data organizations.

- Strong executive communication, presentation, and stakeholder management skills.

- Ability to balance strategic thinking with hands-on execution.

Preferred Qualifications
- Experience supporting advanced analytics, machine learning, or AI-enabled business solutions.

- Experience within financial services or another highly regulated industry.

- Advanced degree or relevant industry certifications.

Keys to Success in this Role:
- Think strategically while driving measurable business outcomes.

- View governance as a business enabler that increases trust, transparency, and responsible data use.

- Build strong relationships and influence decisions across business and technology organizations.

- Translate complex governance, data, and AI concepts into actionable solutions.

- Balance innovation, consumer experience, and risk management.

- Drive alignment and accountability without relying on organizational authority.

- Lead through collaboration, credibility, and execution.

- Maintain a relentless focus on building trusted, AI-ready data that can scale across Multifamily's growing consumer community.

Position Overview:
Are you passionate about counterparty credit risk management? We're looking for someone who can navigate complex credit challenges across banks and corporates — identifying, measuring, and managing risk while delivering solutions that are innovative, thorough, and practicable. If that sounds like you, come join our team! You’ll have the opportunity to assess the credit strength of counterparties and perform financial continuous due-diligence activities, while playing an active role in the development of methodologies and related risk reporting on counterparty matters. Apply now and learn why there’s #MoreAtFreddieMac!

Our Impact:
- Our team is responsible for managing Freddie Mac’s counterparty credit risk exposure to Banks and Corporates.
- Ensure that counterparty risks are adequately evaluated, and that adverse portfolio and/or individual counterparty trends are identified in a proactive manner.

Your Impact:
- Assess on an ongoing basis the creditworthiness of Banks and Corporate counterparties.
- Assign internal counterparty ratings and document the corresponding rationale similar to a rating agency credit opinion.
- Conduct due diligence on new counterparty applicants as needed as part of internal approval processes.
- Develop recommendations for corrective actions to address counterparty non-compliance.
- Assist in the development and improvement of counterparty eligibility requirements and related policies and procedures.
- Manage and monitor internal counterparty risk exposures against corporate limits.
- Conduct credit risk analyses of emerging industry issues and industry trends.
- Find opportunities for operational improvement that streamline or improve existing processes.
- Perform periodic management reporting related to counterparty credit risk and assist in developing presentations to senior management.

Qualifications:
- BS/BA Degree in finance, economics, accounting, or a related degree or equivalent along with 5+ years of related professional work experience in financial services, consulting, risk management, or a related field
- 3+ year of Counterparty experience
- Ability to assess a company’s financial strength through analyzing its financial documents, statements, and other related materials
- Proficient in MS Office with advanced skills in Excel

Keys to Success in this Role:
- Excellent analytical skills
- Good verbal and written communication skills
- Ability to work independently with limited direct supervision
